docs.title: PyKampala Community Blog
docs.text:
Welcome to the PyKampala Community Blog — technical stories, tutorials, and community updates from Python developers in Uganda. Established 2016.

We host physical and virtual meetups every last Saturday of the month. This blog extends our main website with in-depth articles you can read, share, and discuss.

Browse All Posts → ← Back to PyKampala Community

docs.title: Latest Posts
docs.text:
The newest articles appear first. Read the preview of the blog and follow the link to read more.

docs.title: Why Project Structure Matters
docs.text:
A well-structured Python project saves time, prevents bugs, and makes collaboration joyful. In this post, we explore a minimal yet scalable layout inspired by real Pykampala contributions.

A clear layout is documentation for your future self.

docs.title: A Minimal Layout
docs.text:
my_project/
├── src/
│   └── my_package/
│       ├── __init__.py
│       └── core.py
├── tests/
│   └── test_core.py
├── pyproject.toml
└── README.md

docs.title: Packaging with pyproject.toml
docs.text:
[project]
name = "my_package"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "An example Python package"
requires-python = ">=3.9"

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
def test_core():
    from my_package.core import hello
    assert hello("Kampala") == "Hello, Kampala!"

Run with:

pytest

docs.title: Images in Posts
docs.text:
Place images under content/blog/assets/ and reference them:

![Diagram](assets/my-diagram.png)

Alt text is required for accessibility — describe what the image conveys.
